issuing_body: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
title: Minn. Stat. § 256B.12 — Legal Representation
supports: Minnesota law authorizes the Attorney General or the appropriate county attorney, acting independently or at the Attorney General's direction, to institute criminal or civil actions to prosecute specified Medicaid/public-assistance offenses or recover wrongfully made Medicaid payments.
2026 Minn. Laws ch. 127 art. 7 § 2 updates the cross-reference from former § 609.466 to new § 609.467, the Medical Assistance Fraud offense.
The neighboring § 609.467 offense is effective August 1, 2026, for crimes committed on or after that date.
important_qualifications: This is subject-specific authority for Medicaid matters and should not be generalized into a claim that the Attorney General has the same direct criminal authority for every state program.
The § 256B.12 amendment and the new § 609.467 offense should be cited with the applicable session-law effective dates when analyzing conduct spanning the 2026 change.
Direct prosecution authority is distinct from DHS's separate administrative authority to suspend or withhold Medicaid payments under § 256B.064.
